1. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.8,75,840/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. In respect of an accident which is not in dispute.

The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
"Head injury with traumatic brain injury, right FTP acute SDH with mild line shift,
right parietal ICH, Bilateral frontal SDH and bilateral Basi frontal contusion, right ear bleeding left normal bleeding"
3. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:

The Tribunal while awarding the said sums, has also come to the conclusion that the claimant had contributed 20% to the accident.
Admittedly, the claimant was pedestrian and the Tribunal has held that he was contributed 20% to the accident even though the charge sheet had been laid against the driver of the insured vehicle.

In my view, having regard to the age of the claimant and the fact that the charge sheet was laid against the driver of the insured vehicle, it is obvious that the attribution of negligence on the claimant is incorrect and the same is accordingly set aside and it is therefore, held that the driver of the insured vehicle alone was responsible for the accident.
5. The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered 45.07% permanent physical impairment and 66.16% to the whole body.
In my view, having regard to the evidence on record, it would be appropriate to take the disability at 60% as against 50% determined by the Tribunal.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.7,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year, 2015 would be Rs.9,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 63 years, a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,53,600/- (Rs.9,000 x 12 x 7 x 60%) towards 'loss of future income' .
8. As a consequence, the amount of Rs.42,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.54,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 6 months).
9. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.40,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.13,51,400/- as against Rs.10,94,800/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
14. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
15. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
16. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
